item.title: Herzog: 'On the eve of Yom Kippur, let us say clearly, terror will not break us'
item.description: President Isaac Herzog said in response to the deadly shooting attack in Binyamin: “The deadly terror attack in Binyamin comes just before Yom Kippur, when the people of Israel gather for the holiest day of the year. I bow my head in memory of the victim murdered in the terror attack. I share wholeheartedly in the grief of his family and community and pray for the recovery of the wounded. On the eve of this sacred festival, let it be stated clearly: Terror will not break us, and it will not shake our spirit. We will stand against terror together, united, resolute, and full of faith."

item.title: Arabs threw stones at Jews in Silwan
item.description:
Police have opened an investigation after Arabs threw stones at a group of young Jews in the Silwan neighborhood of eastern Jerusalem. According to initial investigation, one of the young men, sensing danger, fired into the air to drive the suspects away.
No injuries were reported. The police and Border Police are conducting searches to locate the suspects.

item.title: MDA responds to Neveh Tzuf shooting
item.description:
Magen David Adom personnel provided updates on the terrorist shooting attack in Binyamin.
MDA Paramedic David Trachtenberg said: “We arrived at the scene and saw a male in his 30s inside a vehicle, unconscious, with multiple gunshot wounds. We removed him from the vehicle and immediately began providing life-saving medical treatment. We placed him in the ambulance, and with the assistance of a physician and a paramedic, immediately began evacuating him to the hospital while fighting for his life, providing medical treatment and blood products, in the hope of stabilizing his condition."
MDA EMT Yosef Rimal said: “We received a report of a man who had been injured by gunfire. We arrived at the scene with a large number of forces and found the man unconscious. We immediately began providing advanced medical treatment, including controlling bleeding, bandaging and administering medications, and evacuated him in an MDA ambulance in serious condition."

item.title: Morocco prepares for protests against expanding normalization with Israel
item.description:
The Moroccan Front for Support for Palestine and Against Normalization, a non-governmental organization opposed to ties with Israel, has called for three days of nationwide protests against the deepening and expansion of normalization between the countries. The demonstrations are scheduled for September 25-27.
Protests are expected to be held following Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar's visit to New York, where he met with Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita to promote a further upgrade in relations between Israel and Morocco.
